Sandbox/Survival Mode: (Have no interest in Story Mode)
Never had done any survival games, would probably even say; That's not for me, the stress of time pressure is something I always avoid in games.
Wanted games to be "chill" and not get into problems when I do other stuff at the same time. Until I saw The Long Dark randomly playing at GrayStillPlays channel.

And even though I die (permanently, no saves) so many times in this game, because I don't find food, or shelter or get eaten by a bear (and believe me, that pressure can be overwhelming O.o), it IS the most "chill" game I have ever played.

Because when you find a bit of food, that shelter and there are no bears around just now, you can enjoy every detail The Long Dark offers. The quiet, the art, the sounds and the music. I love every pixel, and I bet I will need many years to see them all.

This is not a game for everybody. If you desire fast action, hyper quick results, loud and rapidly changing visual entertainment in games and not so much having to think/plan about what to do next in a game, then you might not like this one. In every other case: Get.This.Game!

The game is fun, and will last a long time Although it won't be very fun if you just stay in one place trying to just stay alive.
But the bugs...
Suddenly I can't click on anything, losing hours of progress because you didn't do anything that triggers a save, losing your badge progress because "couldn't restore profile" and the best one: losing your whole save of 70+ days TWICE because it crashed while saving.
Buy at your own risk.

I've been really enjoying my experience with this game and have started off with Wintermute story mode, which has allowed me get more familiar with the game and the map. I've been searching for a game that feels like I'm relying only on the environment for survival, where everything is acquired from scratch. I also prefer a game without zombies or enemies, I just want a nice relaxing game. There are wolves and bears but you can adjust the settings so that you never have to interact with them. I do believe there are some exciting opportunities for the game to be more engaging.

While Bear Island offers a challenging environment, it would be intersting to explore other climates, such as a desert or rainforest. This could add a new layer of complexity to the survival experience and provide players with fresh challenges.

Building a custom home base or cabin could be a fantastic feature. Allowing players to create their safe haven and decorate it according to their preferences.

Also, introducing in-game companions like dogs or horses. Dogs could help with tracking, hunting, and protection, while horses could provide faster travel, making exploration more efficient and enjoyable.

Overall, the game has a solid foundation, but these additions could take it to the next level, offering players more variety and opportunities for creativity in their survival journey. I'm excited to see how the developers continue to evolve the game.

A journey about finding inner peace.

The Long Dark is a single player survival game set in a frozen post apocalyptic Canada.

I like the systems, they mostly make sense and I find the 'realism' doesn't detract from the game-play too much. The music is sparse which works well for the loneliness of the setting.

There are lots of areas to explore and each ones feels unique although generally you'll be doing the same thing in each area which comes down to finding food and exploring for loot.

It's a relaxing game most of the time although some areas just have too many wolves that seem to respawn too often and while there are a few ways to deal with them after a while it becomes tedious.

I can't comment on the Story mode as I only played the first chapter and have spent the rest of my time in survival mode.

Over-all a pretty chill game.

This is a spectacular game if you're looking for an immersive realistic survival experience. The solitude you find yourself in as you traverse the frigid environment that is ALWAYS trying to kill you has a way of reinforcing that immersion. The survival mode alone is a masterpiece for the survival genre and there aren't many titles that can replicate it. You will find yourself putting hours into a single run only to die of an infection that you forgot to treat with antibiotics. Becoming more and more skilled with every death, you will find yourself growing in confidence with every attempt. The challenges are super fun tests of your ability to stay alive in this world. The story mode allows beginners to get the hang of the controls while giving you some context on what is actually going on in this desolate, frigid world. Couldn't recommend more.

First of all, I have a craze for survival games.
However, when I laid my eyes on The Long Dark I thought it would be boring.
I loved everything about it, I loved the art, the sound, the setting, the approach from the developers with the community... but I didn't know that I would really like it until I started playing.

Thing gets immersive really fast in this game. I'm used to fast paced stuff but the speed here is not a problem when you need to think what to do with what you have. When you are close to dying it is easy to feel the desperation, something games usually rob you of. Not here tho, you don't want to risk and lose all you did, all you explored, everything you planned. But it will happen, eventually the smallest mistake or a quick judgement will drag you into The Long Dark.
Then you start again, and look for more wild to conquer.

This game is about attention, patience and management. It has it's moments with action, but most of the times you want to avoid it. If you like survivals with tiny details, give this one a try.

(Be Warned) The Long Dark: Iron Road brings in cool ideas like the train, but Anna Island proves Hinterland is getting lazy. Instead of the handcrafted, beautifully detailed maps we got back in Timberwolf Mountain or Ash Canyon, this expansion feels like a massive, empty walking simulator. The terrain is just flat snow with generic, copy-pasted rock spires slapped along the tracks, ugly stretched textures, and terrible collision geometry that breaks your ankles every two steps. Except for the main mountain in the distance that looks decent for screenshots, the whole area around Port Remnant feels rushed and hollow. Following up on Zone of Contamination, it really feels like they traded quality design for empty scale, leaving us with a $30 map that’s more frustrating to trek through than it is fun to play.

If you didn't enjoy Zone of Contamination you may not enjoy this.

I've been following this game since it was first released, and even wrote an article for it on Tumblr waaaay way back to help get it some traction. The game has changed so much since that playthrough I did for the article - in the best possible way. You can tell that the devs care so much about this game and the experience you as a player will have. It is extremely in depth and addictive, and there is always a challenge to test yourself with. I enjoy walking around and coming up with a plan that I can achieve within the day, whether it be looting, hunting, fishing, waiting out storms, creating a base, or trying to travel to another location that will have more lucrative items I need. I highly recommend this game -- you can tell the devs care about it, and it's community cares about it too. 11/10 game

If you want a game to hold your hand and let you finish it in 20 hours, this game isn't for you. There is a little bit of a learning curve, but there are plenty of helpful people on the discussion boards, as well as a wiki and other things. The firearms, if you are an fps player, are a little wonky. Choices and planning matter, then once you have those basics down the game becomes easier. Luckily the game has several different difficulty levels as well as customized levels you can choose. In addition, there are some specific challenges to do within the game, and the steam achievements will keep you going. You will get plenty of playtime with the purchase. The one downside I would want to state upfront, is that the game developers have a roadmap for game updates, but those are targets and I wouldn't want to base any decision to buy based on those moving target dates. Game can be difficult at first if you just wing it instead of watching vids or reading guides.

“The Long Dark” is an immersive and captivating game that has truly captured my attention from the moment I started playing. The game’s stunning graphics and atmospheric sound design create a hauntingly beautiful post-apocalyptic world that feels both eerily familiar and utterly alien.

One of the standout features is the game’s challenging survival mechanics. Managing resources such as food, water, and warmth feels incredibly realistic, making every decision crucial. The dynamic weather and wildlife add an extra layer of tension, keeping you on the edge of your seat as you navigate the frozen wilderness.

The narrative is equally compelling, with a rich and engaging storyline that unfolds as you progress. The game’s ability to blend survival challenges with a deep and intriguing narrative is rare and impressive. It’s not just about staying alive; it’s about understanding the story behind the disaster and the characters you encounter along the way.

Overall, “The Long Dark” is a masterpiece in the survival genre. It offers a deeply satisfying and often harrowing experience that will leave you both exhausted and exhilarated. If you’re a fan of challenging games with a focus on survival and storytelling, this is one you won’t want to miss.

I absolutely love this game, and it's still only in Alpha! I feel totally immersed while I'm playing it; the sound effects are perfect, and I enjoy both the 'exploration' mode and the 'normal' mode. I appreciate that they even HAVE the exploration mode so, so much. Very enjoyable, and super excited for when the story mode finally comes out!

Edit:: Over three years since I wrote this review, and I still absolutely love this game. The developers are attentive to the community, the controls have gotten better, the Story Mode is cool, and the environment and sound effects continue to be top-notch. Absolutely love this game.

Edit 2:: It's now 2022 and the first paid DLC has been released -- and I love the game even more. The studio/developers continue to care deeply about the feedback they receive from the community, and while I haven't gotten too deep into the first part of this year-long DLC release, I'm having a great time exploring another new region on Great Bear Island. The additional music and atmospheric sounds with this expansion are especially lovely, although they have been with each major release. Can't wait for story mode to finally finish!

Edit 3:: still love this game but only updating this for the steam cool points. also the final chapter has an announced release date of march 31st, 2026! yay :D
